observations.title: WorldResolutions::new panics (chunks(0)) for an empty camera plan with worlds > 0
observations.detail: With plan.resolutions empty, stored_resolutions expected = worlds × 0 = 0 and an empty table passes the length check, then resolutions.chunks(plan.resolutions.len()) = chunks(0) panics ('chunk size must be non-zero'). QA reproduced it with catch_unwind (panic caught = true). Empty camera selection is an already-supported scenario in this repository (R08 empty-selection no-op), so nworld > 1 + empty selection would hit this panic in a public API. It is not part of the slice's seven listed error classes, so QA does not call it a blocker for the slice's stated scope, but it should be fixed before R10-S2 uses WorldResolutions with empty selection.
observations.fix_or_accept: FIX (2 lines): return an empty table early when plan.resolutions.is_empty(), or iterate by index instead of chunks(0); fix before S2 wiring.

observations.title: Very large worlds panic while allocating the active mask, so CountOverflow is unreachable through the public API
observations.detail: WorldLayout::resolve, WorldStates::new and WorldStates::with_active allocate vec![true; worlds] / states before any bound check, so an absurd worlds value (e.g., usize::MAX) panics with a capacity overflow instead of returning CountOverflow (QA reproduced with catch_unwind). Consequently CountOverflow { world_offset / world_buffer_elements / world_states } is effectively unreachable through the public API.
observations.fix_or_accept: FIX or ACCEPT: add an explicit upper bound or try_reserve -> CountOverflow, or document that worlds must be allocatable and CountOverflow is defensive-only.

observations.title: WorldLayout::resolve resolves the single-world layout before checking nworld == 0
observations.detail: An invalid plan (single-world layout overflow) combined with nworld == 0 returns WorldError::Layout(ContextError) rather than WorldCountZero; with a valid plan nworld == 0 is correctly rejected. Error precedence is not documented.
observations.fix_or_accept: ACCEPT (correct rejection for valid plans) or FIX by checking nworld == 0 first / documenting the precedence.
